div.p: The school famously synthesized Marxist economic theory with Freudian psychoanalysis. They were interested in why the working class did not revolt as Marx had predicted. They looked to psychology to understand how societal pressures and authority structures shape the individual's subconscious, leading people to "love their own oppression."

div.p: Adorno and Horkheimer introduced the concept of the "culture industry" to explain how mass-produced popular culture (movies, music, media) functions as a tool of social control. They argued that it keeps the public passive and distracts them from political reality by churning out standardized, "easy" entertainment.

div.p: The Frankfurt School refers to a group of German thinkers associated with the Institute for Social Research at Goethe University Frankfurt, founded in 1923. They are best known for developing Critical Theory, a social philosophy that critiques modern society and culture by examining the structures of power, ideology, and domination.

div.p: Questions I wanted to dig into.

ul.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; padding-inline-start: 23.4px; padding-left: 23.4px; text-align: left; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 32px; min-height: 32px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.p: With all of the breathless proclomations about AI taking all of the jobs, i wanted some historical grounding to see how " technological innovation" had transformed the economy in the past.

li.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 32px; min-height: 32px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.p: I had been listened to a podcast about the Frankfurt School, and particularly about the mechanisms around the alienated worker getting sold back status-quo pop culture, and him/them/her preferring it because it didn't make him uncomfortable/aware about the issues with the status quo. I had heard of the term "The Great Refusal" as Marcuse's potential solution to this problem posed by Adorno and wanted to explore it. I also wanted to see whether the further "democratization of creating media" effects of AI tools could relate to the mechanisms of this

li.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 32px; min-height: 32px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.p: As an artist working in the technology industry, both of these lines of thought seemed linked to me in terms of "how might things changing economically, and how can we influence culture so that they change for the better".

li.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 32px; min-height: 32px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.p: I wanted to merge economic/social-science history + lefty theory to drive praxis with technical chops using current AI tools

div.p: Avneesh's opinions on using AI tools for research

ul.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; padding-inline-start: 17.550001px; padding-left: 17.550001px; text-align: left; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.p: Overall, a benefit of non-ai research is to find things you might not have been looking for, so be careful about any kind of directional bias in your prompts (eg, separating summaries from analysis in workflow setup)

ul.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; list-style-type: circle; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; padding-inline-start: 17.550001px; padding-left: 17.550001px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.p: In general, being aware of summarize vs analyze continuum and being sensitive to pushing back on AI attempts to analyze when appropriate - depends how and what kind of thinking you are intentionally offloading to AI

li.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.p: IMO Survey research is best done in service to some specific goal, but then the tasks offloaded to AI should be one step below the top level synthesis - the top level goal keeps your human intention and criticality sharp enough (you can feel the friction between the top level goal and the results of the deferred goal pursued by the AI) and this feels like a decent bang for buck safeguard when you’ve already committed to using AI heavily

li.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

p.style: box-sizing: border-box; color: rgb(29, 29, 29); color-scheme: light; margin-block: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; margin-top: 0px; min-block-size: 24px; min-height: 24px; text-rendering: optimizelegibility; unicode-bidi: isolate;

li.p: There is no such thing as an objective reading of the text - so when comparing AI vs human summary, you just have to be aware of the different colorings - (vague potential inaccuracy vs idiosyncratic directionality?)
